newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent trades lower again, other grades hold.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent trades lower again, other grades hold.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Dated Brent remained weak on Tuesday despite a recovery in outright paper prices, but other North Sea grades stood on firmer ground.
Dated Brent traded again at Nov paper -8 cts for an Oct 11-13 loader, the same level as on Monday, after trading at parity early on Tuesday for an Oct 15-17 cargo.
Dealers said Dated differentials would stay under pressure while the transatlantic arbitrage remained closed.
They said Tuesday's parity trade was to a refiner willing to pay a small premium for specific, and later, loading dates.
Both Oct 16-18 Brent dates were kept on Tuesday, one each by BP and Stasco.
Premiums for Oseberg, Statfjord and Forties remained steady at higher levels traded recently.
Spread play saw Nov/Dec Brent settle back to about +45 cents after gaining 10 cents to +50 cents as outright November regained its losses to $23.20 a barrel.
Sour Urals rose in the Mediterranean after a European trader bought three cargoes on Monday following weather-related loading delays and pipeline repairs at Black Sea outlet Novorossiisk.
Two of the cargoes -- two 80,000 tonners and one of 130,000 tonnes all purchased at about Dated Brent -60 cts cif Med -- were expected to be reoffered on the market.
One of the smaller vessels initially asked Dated Brent -50 cts on Tuesday.
Urals was also priced higher in northern Europe after a traded at Dated Brent -53 cts cif NWE.
